value.rationale: The precise natural fixed-order MIS relaxation problem is motivated by the two-sweep universal bound. Its exact first-entry census is a nontrivial weighted-transfer computation; asymptotically almost every initial state needs the second pass. The measurable dynamic contrast is not a routine restatement of the classical bound or the Perrin fixed-point count.
